items.justification: Publishing the rationale for absent updates versus secure software supply chain processes.
Encryption of sensitive personal data in transit versus accessible user guidance on system configuration.
Transparency about hardware replacement support versus evaluating model outputs for unintended influence.
Confidentiality of data in transit versus the permissions an AI system holds on connected systems.
Both ensure security fixes can reach the deployed product; A mandates updateable components, B the provision and delivery of patches.
Replaceability of cryptographic primitives versus security testing before release.
Both govern delivery of security updates; A adds the timeliness obligation, B the notification chain through operators to end-users.
Disabling debug interfaces versus re-testing after a major system update.
Orderly network reconnection versus an audit log of model configuration changes.
Both pursue continuity of service under disruption, A by designed-in resilience to outages, B by recovery planning against attacks.
Both close channels through which internals can be extracted, A the debug interface, B the model output.
Both require ongoing monitoring for security problems, A specifically of telemetry, B of the system infrastructure at large.
Deletion of personal data from services versus log analysis for model anomalies.
Disabling debug interfaces versus maintaining an asset inventory.
Confidentiality in transit and secure deletion at decommissioning cover different stages of one data protection lifecycle.
Publishing a vulnerability disclosure policy versus secure deletion on decommissioning.
Physical protection of debug ports versus tooling for tracking and version-controlling AI assets.
Encryption of personal data in transit versus the security content of model documentation.
Recording why a provision is unmet and assessing a provider's adherence are different obligations that together demonstrate conformance across the supply chain.
Memory access control is an exploit mitigation, not a data confidentiality control; B concerns unauthorized access to training data.
Recording justifications for non-applicable provisions versus staff threat awareness.
Least privilege at runtime versus the business case assessment preceding an AI system.
Activation of automatic updates versus continuous infrastructure monitoring against risk appetite.
Setup guidance for consumers versus preview access that lets operators evaluate model changes.
Password use in machine-to-machine authentication versus log analysis for model drift and poisoning.
Input validation prevents manipulation and restorable known good state recovers from it; together they form the response to system manipulation.
Automating an update mechanism versus selecting risk controls against corporate risk tolerance.
Confidentiality of security parameters on the wire versus an organizational review of access control frameworks; B does not name credential protection.
Recognizable device designation and a maintained asset inventory are the outward and inward halves of asset identification.
Lifecycle management of security parameters versus the patch delivery chain.
Confidentiality of security parameters over the network versus sharing test findings with operators.
Both concern how security updates reach the user; A through consented automation, B through proactive notification.
Cryptographic agility versus robustness of the model to adversarial input; different failure modes.
Encryption of personal data in transit versus secure coding training for AI developers.
Update timeliness versus an audit log of prompt and configuration changes.
Use of reviewed cryptographic implementations versus logging system and user actions.
Ease of applying an update versus protection of confidential training data and weights.
A secure development process and the specific obligation to strip superfluous model capability both fall under secure development of the artefact.
User control over update notifications versus sanitisation of data and inputs.
Tamper resistance of a hard-coded device identity versus awareness of prohibited use cases.
